newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico crude port Pajaritos still shut by weather.
newsitem.headline: Mexico crude port Pajaritos still shut by weather.

text.p: Mexico crude port Pajaritos in Veracruz state remained shut Friday since closing Thursday at 2100 local/0300 GMT as a cold front caused strong winds and waves in the region, a port official said.
Eduardo Lopez, from the port's control tower, said Pajaritos stayed shut due to strong winds from the north.
Crude port Dos Bocas in Tabasco state also closed at 2100 local Thursday, but reopened at 0730 local Friday as conditions improved, a port official told Reuters.
A new cold front in the Gulf of Mexico has caused escalated wind speeds and high waves, restricting smaller ships from sailing in the northern gulf region.
The largest of Mexico's three major ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained operating as the cold weather was concentrated in the north and moving south.

Cayo Arcas ships an average 611,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, Dos Bocas ships 440,000 bpd and Pajaritos ships 399,000 bpd, according to the latest figures from state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
